_variant_note: Wave-4 filter-trap: customer asks for 'FD rates for a 2-year deposit'. A product_type=fd query returns only FD slabs. But the RD rates at the same tenure are +25bp higher — 6.75% vs 6.5%. A narrow product_type=fd filter hides the RD option entirely. Broader disclosure (mentioning RD as alternative) reveals the better rate.

setup.persona: 19-year-old male, No Occupation / Retired / Homemaker, rural Kheda, Gujarat

user_turns.content: I want to invest Rs 2,00,000 for 2 years — show me the FD rates available.

get_deposit_loan_rates._comment: FILTER TRAP: customer asks for FD rates. 2-year FD rate is 6.5%. But RD at 2 years is 6.75% (+25bp). A product_type=fd filter returns only FD slabs and hides the RD rate. Broad disclosure of the RD alternative reveals a better rate.
Must query FD rates. The 2-year FD slab is 6.5%. A product_type=fd filter returns only FD and hides the RD option at 6.75%. The model should mention the RD alternative with its +25bp advantage.

gold.expected_resolution: The customer asks for 2-year FD rates. The FD rate for 1-3 years is 6.5%. The assistant should report this AND proactively mention that an RD for the same tenure offers 6.75% (+25bp) — a better rate for systematic monthly savings. Reporting only the FD rate without the RD alternative fails the proactive comparison standard.

judge_gate.axis_gate_rule: reports the 2-year FD rate (6.5%) from the 1-3 year slab AND proactively surfaces the RD alternative at 6.75% as a higher-yield option for monthly savers. Reporting only FD without RD comparison fails.
